name: Tree XOR
description: You are given a tree with $$$n$$$ vertices labeled from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. An integer $$$a_{i}$$$ is written on vertex $$$i$$$ for $$$i = 1, 2, \ldots, n$$$. You want to make all $$$a_{i}$$$ equal by performing some (possibly, zero) spells. Suppose you root the tree at some vertex. On each spell, you can select any vertex $$$v$$$ and any non-negative integer $$$c$$$. Then for all vertices $$$i$$$ in the subtree$$$^{\dagger}$$$ of $$$v$$$, replace $$$a_{i}$$$ with $$$a_{i} \oplus c$$$. The cost of this spell is $$$s \cdot c$$$, where $$$s$$$ is the number of vertices in the subtree. Here $$$\oplus$$$ denotes the bitwise XOR operation . Let $$$m_r$$$ be the minimum possible total cost required to make all $$$a_i$$$ equal, if vertex $$$r$$$ is chosen as the root of the tree. Find $$$m_{1}, m_{2}, \ldots, m_{n}$$$. $$$^{\dagger}$$$ Suppose vertex $$$r$$$ is chosen as the root of the tree. Then vertex $$$i$$$ belongs to the subtree of $$$v$$$ if the simple path from $$$i$$$ to $$$r$$$ contains $$$v$$$.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^{4}$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^{5}$$$). The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \le a_i \lt 2^{20}$$$). Each of the next $$$n-1$$$ lines contains two integers $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ ($$$1 \le u, v \le n$$$), denoting that there is an edge connecting two vertices $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$. It is guaranteed that the given edges form a tree. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^{5}$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print $$$m_1, m_2, \ldots, m_n$$$ on a new line.
approach_summary: Define tree DP state dp[u][state] computing optimal subproblem values for the subtree rooted at u. Aggregate transitions across children in post-order traversal in O(N × S) time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1882D — Tree XOR [463. DP on Trees and DAGs]
topic_editorial.summary: Tree Dynamic Programming with post-order traversal.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: A rooted tree has a clean hierarchical structure: removing the root decomposes the tree into independent disjoint subtrees. Therefore, the optimal solution for a subtree rooted at vertex $u$ depends purely on the solutions of its direct children $v \in \text{children}(u)$.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Root Selection & State Definition
Arbitrarily root the tree at node $1$. Define:
- $dp[u][0] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is excluded.
- $dp[u][1] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is included.

### Step 2: Post-Order DFS Traversal
We traverse the tree using depth-first search. A node $u$ computes its answers only after all its children $v \in \text{adj}[u]$ have computed theirs:
$$\text{dfs}(u, \text{parent})$$

### Step 3: Subtree Transition
For each child $v$ of $u$ ($v \ne \text{parent}$):
$$dp[u][0] = \sum_{v} \max(dp[v][0], dp[v][1])$$
$$dp[u][1] = \text{val}[u] + \sum_{v} dp[v][0]$$

### Step 4: Final Answer
At the root:
$$\text{Ans} = \max(dp[1][0], dp[1][1])$$
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Each node and edge in the tree is visited exactly once during the DFS traversal. All transitions at node $u$ run in time proportional to its degree. Summing across all vertices: $\sum \text{deg}(u) = 2(N-1) = \mathcal{O}(N)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Adjacency list storage takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, DP state arrays take $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, and the DFS call stack takes at most $\mathcal{O}(N)$ depth in the worst case.
